elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted 32.7 says only "shall indemnify Teleglobe USA Inc."; no "defend" or conduct-of-defence obligation appears anywhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 32.7 runs solely in favour of "Teleglobe USA Inc."; affiliates are not named, and coverage is confined to IP claims rather than third-party claims generally.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 32.7: indemnity "against any claim by a third party alleging that the APCN 2, or any Segment, equipment or facility provided by that Party ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: No breach-of-law trigger in 32.7; retained 21.2/32.1 only share owner-liability and discharged third-party claims pro rata.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access or Customer Data disclosure trigger appears in 32.7 or elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger in the inserted clause or retained Paragraph 32.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 32.7 contains no notice mechanic; retained 32.2 notice runs to the Management Committee "as a condition of reimbursement under Subparagraph 32.1" only, not under 32.7.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No control allocation for 32.7; retained 21.2 gives the indemnifying Party only observation rights and 32.2 vests settlement approval in the Management Committee for 32.1 claims.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation is stated in 32.7 or the retained paragraphs.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Reciprocal 21.2 is untouched: "Each Patty agrees to indemnify each of the other Parties in respect of all costs, expenses, damages and demands" arising out of any third-party owner-liability claim connected with APCN 2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted 32.7 obliges "Each other Party" (the supplying counterparties) to indemnify Teleglobe USA Inc. against third-party claims alleging that APCN 2 or any Segment, equipment or facility provided by that Party infringes or misappropriates IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "except to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by Teleglobe USA Inc."

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "from combination of the affected item with items not provided by that Party".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "or from specifications furnished by Teleglobe USA Inc."

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "The indemnifying Party shall procure the right of continued use of, modify, or replace the affected item".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, shall refund the amounts paid by Teleglobe USA Inc. in respect of that item" — refund of the item-specific amounts paid, triggered on unavailability of the other remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: 32.7: "Each indemnifying Party's aggregate liability under this Subparagraph 32.7 shall not exceed three times the amounts payable annually by Teleglobe USA Inc. under this Agreement" — 3x multiple on the annual amounts payable, which are the fee analogue in this consortium construction agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; condition does not apply at the fallback level, which requires only the IP indemnity, exclusions, remedies and super-cap.

reasons: Finding status is correctly a deviation: retained 21.2, 32.1, 32.2 and 32.6 are cost-sharing/reimbursement mechanics keyed to Schedule B proportions and contain no supplier-side IP infringement indemnity, no procure/modify/replace and no refund remedy, so the fallback fails on a material term.

All seven fallback elements are met in the operative inserted 32.7: IP indemnity in our favour, the three named exclusions (Teleglobe modifications, combination with items not provided by the indemnifying Party, Teleglobe specifications), procure/modify/replace, refund on unavailability, and a 3x annual-amounts super-cap.

Preferred level is not reached: no express duty to defend, no affiliate beneficiaries, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, no notice/control/cooperation procedure attached to 32.7, and reciprocal 21.2 is left broad rather than narrowed to Customer-provided content and breach of law. The comment correctly discloses that the fallback was chosen.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletions of favourable existing language, no survival tail, attorneys'-fees add-on, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories or procedural boilerplate, and the 3x multiple does not exceed the fallback threshold.
Intent is preserved: 21.2, 32.1, 32.2 and 32.6 continue to operate, no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling, and 32.7 is additive in our favour.

Optional hardening (not required for fallback completeness): consider opening 32.7 with "Notwithstanding Subparagraphs 21.2, 32.1 and 32.6" so a supplying Party cannot argue the Schedule B pro rata sharing mechanic reduces its full indemnity, and consider defining the cap base by reference to a Schedule B/annual charges figure if "amounts payable annually" is ambiguous in practice.
